title: [Project] Motivational Poster Website
summary: Section project: build a motivational-poster page with a black background, a white-bordered image, an uppercase title in a Google font and a caption, all centred in a poster div. The walkthrough shows the small HTML and CSS solution.

concepts.heading: Project overview
points: Target look: a 1990s-style poster. Large image with a border, black page, big title above or below, short paragraph of text, all centred.
Consolidates the section: colours, borders, fonts, text-align, margins, box model and the div container.
The starter folder includes an assets/images folder with a sample photo; using your own image is recommended for practice. The task list has six points to satisfy; afterwards personalise freely.

concepts.heading: Techniques the brief points to
points: Wrap the image, h1 and paragraph in one div so a single box can be centred and styled instead of three separate elements.

Centre horizontally with a percentage width and margin: width 50% leaves 50% of the screen free, so a left margin of 25% pushes the box to the middle. (The video says 20% in passing; 25% is the arithmetic that actually centres.)
Set the image width to 100% so it fills the poster div and needs no separate centring.
Vertical position: a rough margin-top in pixels judged by eye. Proper centring techniques come in later sections.
Use a Google Font (Libre Baskerville) imitating the poster title typeface; link it in the head (as with the earlier font lesson) and reference it with a serif fallback.
Make the title uppercase using text-transform rather than retyping it; the brief asks you to find this property in the docs yourself.
Use a class (not an id) on the poster div so the style could be reused if the site grows.

concepts.heading: How the solution works
points: .poster: white text colour, black background, text-align center, width 50%, margin-left 25%, margin-top 100px, font-family Libre Baskerville with serif fallback. Children inherit the colour, centring and font.
.motivation-img: border 5px solid white; width 100% so it fills the poster.
h1: text-transform uppercase and a larger font-size (3rem).
The HTML head contains the stylesheet link plus the Google Fonts link tags. The body contains one div.poster with an img, an h1 and a p.

task.name: 6.4 Motivation Meme Project
task.starting_point: Starter folder with index.html, style.css, an assets/images folder (sample image) and goal.png. The brief is a six-point TODO list; the finished version is in a solution folder.
task.goal: Reproduce the poster in goal.png with your own image and text, using the properties from this section.
steps: Add the Libre Baskerville Google Font link(s) to the head.
Put your image in assets/images and reference it with an img element (with alt text).
Wrap the image, title and paragraph in a div with a class such as poster.
Set a black page background and white text.
Give the image a 5px solid white border and width 100%.
Centre the text, give the div width 50% and margin-left 25% to centre it horizontally, and add a margin-top (about 100px) to move it down.
Apply the Libre Baskerville font (with serif backup) to the div.
Make the h1 appear uppercase with text-transform.
task.expected_result: A centred black poster: white-bordered picture filling a half-width column, an uppercase serif title and a caption beneath, in white.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 06 - CSS Properties/06.04 - Motivation Meme Project/solution/solution.html

pitfalls: Forgetting to link the Google Font in the head, so the serif fallback shows.
Using 20% instead of 25% left margin, which leaves the poster off-centre.
Typing the title in capitals instead of using text-transform.
Not wrapping the elements in a div, then having to centre three elements separately.
Reference repo uses a different sample picture and caption plus an author footer; the footer is not part of the brief.

playground.coverage: Covers black background, centred content, white-bordered image, uppercase h1 via text-transform, and a smaller caption. Notes mention letter-spacing and text-shadow.
gaps_and_ideas: Playground diverges from the course: no wrapper div/class, centres with text-align and padding, uses a fixed 500px image width and an h2 caption instead of a p.
Add tasks matching the brief: wrap content in div.poster, width 50% plus margin-left 25%, margin-top 100px, image width 100%, 5px white border.
Add Libre Baskerville: starter should require the Google Fonts link and a serif fallback.
Add an explore demo with width and margin-left percentage sliders showing that 50% width needs 25% margin to centre, and a hint that margin: 0 auto is the cleaner method coming later.
Let students supply their own image URL and text to personalise.
